We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 5 reactions for target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We have guidance: steps enumerated forward: TBS protection, HWE, DIBAL-H reduction, TMSOTf protection, Still-Gennari reaction. But we need retrosynthetic steps (reverse). So we need to break down target into precursors via 5 steps, each corresponding to reverse of those forward reactions.

Thus we need to propose a route: Starting from target (with TBS protected alcohols maybe). Actually target includes free OH groups? Let's examine structure: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

It has a primary alcohol (CO) side chain? There's a /C=C(CO)/C meaning a double bond with a CH2OH substituent? Also a terminal carboxylic acid (C(O)=O). Also an ether linking to a cyclic diol? Actually O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/... )C... So there is a cyclic acetal? Not sure.

But we can propose retrosynthesis: Step 5 (last forward) Still-Gennari reaction forms Z-alkene from aldehyde and phosphonate. So reverse: we break a double bond to give aldehyde and phosphonate ester. So we need to identify which double bond corresponds to Still-Gennari. Probably the double bond adjacent to the carboxylic acid? Actually Still-Gennari forms (Z)-alkene from aldehyde and phosphonate. In target we have a conjugated diene with a terminal carboxylic acid. The final step likely forms the C=C-C(O)=O (alpha,beta-unsaturated acid) via Still-Gennari from an aldehyde and a phosphonate (maybe a phosphonate of the acid). So retrosynthetic step: target -> precursor aldehyde + phosphonate.

Step 4 forward: TMSOTf protection of alcohols. So reverse: deprotect TMS to give free OH. So we need to identify TMS-protected alcohol in target? Actually target has free OH groups, not TMS. So maybe the forward route had TMS protection then later deprotection? But we need 5 steps total. The guidance enumerates forward steps: TBS protection, HWE, DIBAL-H, TMSOTf protection, Still-Gennari. That's 5 steps forward. So reverse order: Step 5 (reverse of Still-Gennari) -> gives aldehyde + phosphonate. Step 4 (reverse of TMSOTf protection) -> remove TMS to give free OH (but target already free, so maybe before Still-Gennari there was TMS protection that got removed later? Actually forward order: 1 TBS protection, 2 HWE, 3 DIBAL-H, 4 TMSOTf protection, 5 Still-Gennari. So after step 5 we have final product (target). So reverse: target -> step5 reverse (undo Still-Gennari) -> intermediate with TMS-protected alcohols? Wait step 4 is TMSOTf protection, which occurs before Still-Gennari. So after step 4 we have TMS-protected alcohols, then step5 forms double bond. So reverse: after undoing Still-Gennari we get intermediate with TMS-protected alcohols. Then reverse step4: deprotect TMS to give free OH (maybe after step5 they remain protected? Actually TMS protection before Still-Gennari, so after Still-Gennari the TMS groups remain. So final product may still have TMS groups? But target has free OH, not TMS. So maybe after Still-Gennari they deprotect TMS later, but not listed. However we have only 5 steps, so maybe the target includes TBS protected groups? Actually target has O[C@H]1... that's a free OH attached to carbon. No silyl groups. So maybe the forward steps are different order: TBS protection (protect secondary alcohol), HWE (form double bond), DIBAL-H (reduce ester to aldehyde), TMSOTf protection (protect primary alcohol), Still-Gennari (form Z-alkene). After Still-Gennari we have final product with TMS protected? Not sure.

Given limited time, we can construct a plausible retrosynthetic tree using the templates we have. We need to retrieve template IDs for each transformation. We have one template for TBS deprotection (template 29646). That's reverse of TBS protection: it converts protected to alcohol. So we can use that as step 1 (reverse of TBS protection). Actually forward TBS protection adds TBS; reverse removes TBS. So we can apply template 29646 to target to get precursor with TBS group.

Let's test check if template matches target. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with template_id 29646.
